content.comment_body: Hello, I'm working with a test-station that includes a [product_name] module ([article_no]) and a connected expansion module ([article_no]). There's also a [product_name] operator device set up for HMI purposes. This station is mainly for FAT-testing robot cells, communicating via DeviceNet. DeviceNet communication currently uses a Phoenix module, with signals wired to the [product_name]'s I/O. I'm running into limitations on available outputs with my current configuration and need to expand the signal count in the control logic. I see two potential solutions and would particularly like input on the first: - The machines interfacing with the robots support DeviceNet either natively, with addon cards, or via a gateway (e.g., AnyBus X-Gateway) converting to and from Ethernet/IP. Does [product_name] support Ethernet/IP communication, or would I need a gateway that translates DeviceNet to Modbus? I have no prior experience with Modbus, so I would prefer to avoid it. - Alternatively, adding two more expansion modules could increase I/O capacity. Is this a feasible solution, or does it exceed the expansion limits? If there's an expansion module focused solely on outputs, that might also address my needs since I primarily require additional outputs. Any feedback or suggestions would be appreciated. Please let me know if more details are needed!

Welcome to the forum. The current [product_name] ([version_no]) supports a maximum of 24 digital inputs and 20 digital outputs. The base module offers 8 digital inputs and 4 digital outputs, and each expansion module provides 8 inputs and 8 outputs. Base module: 8 DI, 4 DO 2 x expansion modules: 16 DI, 16 DO Total: 24 DI, 20 DO With this setup, you've reached the maximum expansion limits for this module. On the network side, [product_name] supports communication via Ethernet TCP/IP (using the S7 protocol) and Modbus TCP/IP.

There is uncertainty about supported communication protocols, particularly Ethernet/IP and Modbus, as well as questions regarding hardware expansion limits. The response clarifies technical constraints related to maximum digital I/O and specifies the available communication protocols, guiding the user on system scalability expectations.

They also expect [product_name] to offer flexible network communication options, ideally supporting Ethernet/IP for integration with other equipment, avoiding unfamiliar protocol conversions.
